list.name: Old Hisa
list.text: A Lantern-bearer, at my ferry! Ferry’s been dry for years, dear, but the shop’s open and the futon’s aired.

then.name: Old Hisa
then.text: Funny thing. Every night a little dog sits on my doorstep. Every morning he’s gone. I’ve never once been able to pet him.

br.name: Old Hisa
br.ask: Thirty gold for river fish and a quiet room. Stay the night?

then.name: Old Hisa
then.text: The Kappa at the ford? He’s proud, not cruel. Bring him a cucumber and bow back when he bows. My Oto used to bark at him.

else.name: Old Hisa
else.text: Past the ford is the Hollow, where the Willow Mother weeps. Folk go in there to forget something, and come out forgetting everything.

list.name: Oto
list.text: Wuf.
A small dog with a worn collar sits on the shop step, watching the door. He will not come any closer to the river.

then.name: Mio
then.text: Hisa’s dog. She can’t see him from her Shore.

then.name: Kaze
then.text: The Anchor, Mio. Hold this doorstep for both of them.

br.text: The Anchor holds the doorstep’s Far Shore image in place. For a moment Hisa’s door belongs to both Shores.

br.name: Old Hisa
br.text: …Oto? Oto! Oh, you silly thing, you’ve been here the whole time?
She kneels. Her hand passes through his ears, but he leans into it anyway, tail thumping the step.

br.name: Old Hisa
br.text: Go on, then. You don’t have to wait for me. I’ll find my own way across when it’s time. Goodbye, my good boy.

br.name: Oto
br.text: Wuf.
Oto does not cross. He trots to Mio, drops a tiny bell at her feet, and looks back toward the Hollow.

br.name: Mio
br.text: You want to stay and guide the others across, don’t you?

br.name: Oto
br.text: Wuf!
(Oto’s Bell jingles near things that are hidden on the Far Shore.)

else.text: Oto whines toward the Hollow. The grief from that direction is too loud right now; any Anchor here would slip.

then.text: The Anchor holds the doorstep’s Far Shore image in place. For a moment Hisa’s door belongs to both Shores.

then.name: Old Hisa
then.text: …Oto? Oto! Oh, you silly thing, you’ve been here the whole time?
She kneels. Her hand passes through his ears, but he leans into it anyway, tail thumping the step.

then.name: Old Hisa
then.text: Go on, then. You don’t have to wait for me. I’ll find my own way across when it’s time. Goodbye, my good boy.

then.text: Wuf.
Oto does not cross. He trots to Mio, drops a tiny bell at her feet, and looks back toward the Hollow.

then.name: Mio
then.text: You want to stay and guide the others across, don’t you?

then.name: Oto
then.text: Wuf!
(Oto’s Bell jingles near things that are hidden on the Far Shore.)

else.text: The image wavers and slips. The grief from the Hollow is too loud right now.

list.name: Oto
list.text: Wuf!
Oto guards the path to the ford, waiting for the next lost traveller.

list.name: Oto
list.text: Wuf! Wuf!
Oto barks at Kaze, and keeps barking, until Kaze takes three steps back.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: …He doesn’t like me much. Dogs can tell things.

list.name: Mio
list.text: Tell what?

list.name: Kaze
list.text: Nothing. Let’s go home. Sachi will want to see the wick.
The river smells of cold stone. Mio stops at the edge.

list.name: Mio
list.text: Kaze, what did we eat this morning?

list.name: Kaze
list.text: …Rice? No. Granny Sachi made… I don’t remember.

list.name: Mio
list.text: Me neither. And I was so hungry.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: The river’s already working on us. Let’s not stand here long.
On the Far Shore a plank bridge spans the river, but it drifts: here, then a little downstream, then here again.

br.text: Mio sets the Anchor Stone on the first plank. The bridge stops drifting and settles, solid, across the river.

else.name: Mio
else.text: An Anchor might hold it for a moment, but a moment isn’t enough to cross. I need something that won’t drift at all.

then.name: Kaze
then.text: The Grove keeper, north of the statues. Ask the Heron.

fieldList.text: The bridge holds for one breath, then slides downstream again.

br.text: Mio sets the Anchor Stone on the first plank. The bridge stops drifting and settles, solid, across the river.

else.name: Mio
else.text: Something heavier. Something that never drifts.

list.text: The Anchor Stone sits on the first plank, perfectly still.

list.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
list.text: Halt! This is the Toll-Ford. All who cross into the Hollow pay the toll: a coin, a cucumber, or a bout!
The Kappa bows very low, carefully, so the water in his head-dish does not spill.

then.name: Tip
then.text: Kappas are proud. Offer a Cucumber in Parley to win the bout at once; a Gale strike spills his dish. Bow back (Guard) when he bows.

then.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
then.text: That coin… I know that coin. Yoshi. He crossed with his sick sister and never paid. I never collected.

br.text: Mio presses the worn coin into the Kappa’s webbed hand.

br.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
br.text: Yoshi’s coin. Yoshi, who carried his sister across on his back and never paid. Paid in full.

br.name: Yoshi
br.text: Then I can go. I can finally go.
The pilgrim smiles and walks into the river light. The Kappa blinks, slowly, as if he has just forgotten something.

br.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
br.text: Keep it. A debt unpaid is a debt remembered. I would rather remember him.

br.name: Yoshi
br.text: Then I’ll stay. Someone ought to watch the ford with you.
The pilgrim takes his place by the ford, a grey guard with a kind face.

br.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
br.text: A bout, then! Mind my dish. If it spills, I sulk for a century.

win.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
win.text: Hah! Hah! A fair fall. Pass, Lantern-bearer, and pass proudly.

then.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
then.text: How did you even… never mind. A bout!

br.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
br.text: A bout, then! Mind my dish. If it spills, I sulk for a century.

win.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
win.text: Hah! Hah! A fair fall. Pass, Lantern-bearer, and pass proudly.

list.name: Kappa Toll-Keeper
list.text: The Willow Mother sings her children’s names and forgets them as fast as she sings. Be kind to her. She was kind to me once.
A grey pilgrim stands at the riverbank, holding nothing. He looks at the ford as though he has forgotten how to want to cross.

br.text: Mio ties the knotted cord around his wrist. A thread of light runs from it into the forest, into the mist, along the river.

br.name: Mio
br.text: Three places. His name is in three places.

else.name: Kaze
else.text: Hollowed. The Rustle Sprites say a name can be tied back on.

then.name: Yoshi
then.text: Yoshi. My name is Yoshi. I carried my sister across this river, and I never paid the Kappa. He never asked.

then.name: Yoshi
then.text: Take this. I’ve held it a hundred years. You decide what it’s for.

else.name: Yoshi
else.text: Talk to the Kappa. Whatever you decide, I’ll stand by it.
The cord tugs toward places he has been. (memories found: see the quest log)

list.name: Yoshi
list.text: Someone ought to watch the ford. I don’t mind. I remember who I am now.

lines: At the ford, long ago: the young pilgrim, soaked to the waist, sets his sister on the far bank. The Kappa watches and says nothing.
She does not wake. Yoshi stays by the river so long that he forgets to leave, and then forgets his name.

then.text: The cord at Mio’s wrist pulls gently east, toward the Crossing.

else.text: The thread of light dims, then points somewhere else.

list.text: A child spirit kneels by the water, calling across it. “Ma? Ma?” Nobody answers. The river carries the word away and does not bring it back.

list.name: Mio
list.text: Willow Hollow is where the river comes from. Whatever’s making everyone forget… it’s in there.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: Sounds like someone who lost her kids. And never stopped looking.
The chest is empty.
The chest is empty.
